text:
Predicates:
AllowedPets(x) ::: Pets are allowed in building x.
DepositRequired(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in building x.
DepositAmount(x, y) ::: The deposit amount in building x is y.
Pets(y) ::: y is a pet.
Cats(y) ::: y is a cat.
ApartmentIn(y, x) ::: y is an apartment in building x.
Rent(y) ::: y is the monthly rent.
WillRent(x, y) ::: Person x will rent apartment y.
MoveInWith(x, y) ::: Person x can move in with pet y.
XMoreThanY(x, y) ::: x is more than y.
XAtMostY(x, y) ::: x is at most y.
Fluffy ::: Fluffy.
Tom ::: Tom.
OliveGarden ::: The Olive Garden.
Premises:
Pets(Fluffy) ∧ Cats(Fluffy) ∧ ApartmentIn(OliveGarden) ∧ Rent(OliveGarden, 2000) ∧ AllowedPets(OliveGarden) ::: Fluffy is a cat, pets are allowed in Olive Garden, and Olive Garden has a rent of $2000.
DepositRequired(OliveGarden) ::: A deposit is required to rent in Olive Garden.
DepositAmount(OliveGarden, d) ::: The deposit amount in Olive Garden is d.
XMoreThan(2000, 1500) ::: The rent of $2000 is more than $1500.
WillRent(Tom, y) ↔ (MoveInWith(Tom, Fluffy) ∧ DepositAmount(OliveGarden, d) ∧ XAtMostY(d, 1500)) ::: Tom will rent if and only if he can move in with Fluffy and the deposit is no more than $1500.
Conclusion:
¬WillRent(Tom, OliveGarden) ::: Tom will not rent an apartment in the Olive Garden.
